name: Jordan
sources: GDP $4.16bn and population 3.62m: World Bank WDI, NY.GDP.MKTP.CD and SP.POP.TOTL, Jordan, 1990. The dollar figure is low because the dinar lost roughly half its value between October 1988 and 1989; Jordan defaulted on its external debt in 1989 and entered an IMF programme.
Inflation 16.2%: World Bank FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG, 1990, down from 25.7% in the crisis year 1989.
Interest rate 8.5% is the Central Bank of Jordan's rediscount rate, entered as an estimate: the World Bank publishes no lending-rate series for Jordan in this period.

Tax 18.0% of GDP: World Bank GC.TAX.TOTL.GD.ZS, 1990. Total central government revenue excluding grants was 25.3% (GC.REV.XGRT.GD.ZS); the gap is Gulf and American transfers, which the Gulf crisis was about to cut off.
Defence 7.8% of GDP: World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS, 1990.

Debt 128.8% of GDP is central government debt: World Bank GC.DOD.TOTL.GD.ZS, 1990. Total external debt was 211.2% of GNI that year (DT.DOD.DECT.GN.ZS, $8.33bn), the highest ratio of any nation in this roster.
Investment: gross fixed capital formation 25.1% of GDP (NE.GDI.FTOT.ZS, 1990), split 10.0 public and 15.1 private.
Oil 0.0: Jordan produces essentially none. The Hamzah field near Azraq yielded a few hundred barrels a day and was shut in the 1990s; Our World in Data records zero for 1990.

Authoritarianism 0.55 is below the electoral ceiling on purpose. King Hussein held martial law powers and appointed every prime minister, but the 8 November 1989 election was the first in twenty-two years and was genuinely contested; the model should let Jordan vote again in 1993, as it did.
Stability 52 is the April 1989 Ma'an bread riots, the IMF austerity programme that caused them, and a treasury that had just defaulted.

Separatism 0.22: Palestinians were a majority or near-majority of the population, and Jordan had renounced its legal claim to the West Bank on 31 July 1988, leaving the question of who Jordan is for unresolved.
Military index 5: about 85,000 men, well trained and British-patterned, but a single armoured division's worth of combat power against neighbours with ten times the mass.
